newsitem.title: USA: Florsheim boosted by operating efficiency.
newsitem.headline: Florsheim boosted by operating efficiency.

text.p: Florsheim Group Inc said Wednesday that improved operating efficiencies helped it report a fourth-quarter profit compared to a year-ago loss.

"The profit trend improved dramatically during the fourth quarter," said chairman Charles Campbell. "Gross margin improvements, due to reduced product costs and improved operating efficiencies, and operating expense reductions attributable to cost containment and cost reductions, significantly boosted our profitability."
The shoe manufacturer reported fourth-quarter earnings of $0.28 a share compared to a year-ago loss of $0.35 a share.
The 1996 quarterly results include a pretax gain from the sale of the company's Hy-Test business.

Campbell said interest expense was lower in 1996 than the prior year because cash generated by the sale of the Hy-Test business in March 1996 repaid $17.6 million in borrowings under the company's credit facility.

During the quarter, Campbell said, "We believe that our U.S. specialty stores posted a higher same-store sales performance than in the comparable period of 1995 than our industry competitors. However, the sales trend for U.S. Wholesale (a company division) was a disappointment."

Campbell added, "While we shipped our first golf shoes and John Deere boot orders late in the quarter, customer fill-in and new shoe shipments were down due to reduced product availability in some categories." He said the order backlog at year-end 1996 was up over 30 percent from the prior year.
In addition, Florsheim said it expects to complete the previously announced sale of its former corporate headquarters building in early 1997.
